action: Re-approach RoboRide regional fleet operations with a specific, numbers-forward pitch now that their Millfield expansion is publicly announced. Howard drafts a one-page capabilities summary — not a letter of interest, a vendor proposal — that lists his current inventory of brake consumables, filters, lubricants, and sensors with unit pricing and next-day local delivery capacity. He calls the regional fleet ops contact, references the prior outreach, and frames the timing explicitly: 'You just announced residential expansion and a delivery partnership. That means more vehicles running more miles in this zip code. I am ten minutes from your nearest maintenance lot and I can have brake pads on their bench by tomorrow morning.' The goal is a trial order or a meeting with their fleet maintenance supervisor. This is the highest-leverage move available given the timing of their expansion announcement.
